items.title: PL/SQL Migration Strategy
items.description: The strategy for migrating 340 PL/SQL packages containing core business logic to Azure is undefined.

items.title: PL/SQL Migration Strategy Clarification
items.description: Will the 340 PL/SQL packages be rewritten into application-tier microservices or converted to PostgreSQL pgSQL?
items.why_it_matters: Rewriting logic in Java/Kotlin significantly increases development effort, whereas database-level conversion impacts database engine selection and performance.

items.title: PL/SQL Conversion to pgSQL
items.description: We assume the PL/SQL logic will be migrated to Azure Database for PostgreSQL using automated conversion tools with manual remediation.
items.impact_if_wrong: If a complete rewrite to Java microservices is required, the project timeline will extend by at least 12 months and require additional development resources.

items.title: Batch Job Orchestration in Azure
items.description: The target orchestration tool and architecture for the 47 Control-M overnight batch jobs are not specified.

items.title: Batch Orchestration Tooling
items.description: Should the 47 batch jobs be migrated to an Azure-native orchestrator like Azure Data Factory, or will Control-M be retained in Azure?
items.why_it_matters: This determines the licensing costs, infrastructure design, and the effort required to redesign the batch execution flow.

items.title: Azure-Native Batch Orchestration
items.description: We assume the batch jobs will be modernized using Azure Data Factory and Azure Batch, eliminating the dependency on Control-M.
items.impact_if_wrong: If Control-M must be retained, we will need to provision and license Control-M agents in Azure, increasing operational costs.

items.title: Phased Migration Coexistence Pattern
items.description: The specific phasing strategy and the required coexistence architecture between on-premises and Azure are undefined.

items.title: Phased Migration Strategy
items.description: What is the preferred dimension for phasing the migration (e.g., by Line of Business, regional branches, or policyholder segments)?
items.why_it_matters: The phasing dimension dictates the design of temporary data synchronization bridges and integration routing during the transition period.

items.title: Phasing by Line of Business
items.description: We assume the migration will be phased by Line of Business (starting with Motor), requiring a bidirectional data replication bridge between Oracle and Azure.
items.impact_if_wrong: If a different phasing strategy is chosen, the data replication architecture and temporary integration interfaces must be completely redesigned.

items.title: Broker SOAP Gateway Implementation
items.description: The architectural approach for maintaining backward compatibility for the 23 legacy SOAP services is not finalized.

items.title: SOAP Gateway Architecture
items.description: Will the legacy SOAP services be exposed via an Azure API Management SOAP-to-REST facade, or do they require hosting a legacy SOAP engine in Azure?
items.why_it_matters: This affects the complexity of the API gateway configuration, security token translation (X.509), and the overall integration footprint.

items.title: APIM SOAP-to-REST Facade
items.description: We assume Azure API Management will be used as a SOAP-to-REST/SOAP-pass-through gateway to expose the legacy interfaces without modifying the core application.
items.impact_if_wrong: If APIM cannot handle the complex WS-Security/X.509 token translation, a custom-built Java SOAP proxy service must be developed and maintained.

items.title: Network Connectivity and Bandwidth
items.description: The availability and capacity of network connectivity between the Oslo data centre and Azure regions are not specified.
items.impact_if_wrong: If ExpressRoute provisioning is delayed or not budgeted, data replication performance will suffer, risking the Q3 2028 migration deadline.

items.title: Azure ExpressRoute Availability
items.description: Is there an active Azure ExpressRoute connection with sufficient bandwidth between the Oslo data centre and Azure Norway East?
items.why_it_matters: Sufficient bandwidth is critical for the phased migration data replication and the daily batch transfers during the coexistence phase.
items.impact_if_wrong: If ExpressRoute provisioning is delayed or not budgeted, data replication performance will suffer, risking the Q3 2028 migration deadline.

items.title: ExpressRoute Provisioning Required
items.description: We assume a new 10 Gbps Azure ExpressRoute connection must be provisioned and configured as part of the project enablement phase.
items.impact_if_wrong: If ExpressRoute provisioning is delayed or not budgeted, data replication performance will suffer, risking the Q3 2028 migration deadline.
